intro: A retrieval engine can avoid scanning every document by storing where each term occurs. Positional postings also preserve the evidence needed for phrase queries.
task: Build positional postings that recover every occurrence of a term while preserving original document IDs.
requirements: documents is a list or tuple of at most 1000 documents; each document is a list or tuple of at most 10000 nonempty string tokens.
Return a dictionary term -> list of [document_id, positions], where positions is a list of zero-based token offsets. Include each document once per term.
Document IDs and positions must be ascending. Empty documents contribute no postings. Matching is exact and case-sensitive.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Group within each document
hints.body: Collect all positions for a term before appending a posting.

hints.title: Keep original document IDs
hints.body: An empty document still occupies its original corpus index.

explanation: A positional inverted index maps vocabulary items back to documents and offsets. Repeated terms produce multiple positions within one posting rather than duplicate document entries.
The construction cost is linear in total token count. This index supplies exact evidence for Boolean and phrase retrieval without assigning a relevance score.
